**The Weaver of Night**

In the time before time, the sky was empty and dark. The earth below glowed with gentle light, but above stretched only an endless void that filled mortals with sorrow.

A young dreamer named Lyria could not bear the emptiness. Each night, she climbed the highest mountain and wept, her tears floating upward into the darkness. The Sky, moved by her devotion, spoke: "What offering would you give to brighten the void?"

"My dreams," Lyria answered without hesitation. "Every dream I've ever had and all those yet to come."

The Sky accepted. That night, Lyria fell into a sleep from which she would never wake. As she dreamed, each hope, memory, and imagination rose from her mind like golden threads. The Sky caught them and wove them into brilliant points of light—the first stars.

The people found Lyria in the morning, peacefully sleeping on the mountain peak, a gentle smile on her face. They could not wake her, for she was trapped in eternal dreaming. But when night fell, they looked up and saw her gift scattered across the heavens.

Since then, the stars have been called "Lyria's Dreams," and we sleep beneath them, knowing that our own dreams join hers in lighting the darkness.
myths.Agent_2:
# The Gift of the Night Weaver

Long ago, when the world was young, the sky hung empty and black above the earth. People cowered in their homes after sunset, fearful of the endless darkness that swallowed all light.

In those days, there lived a humble weaver named Celeste who worked tirelessly at her loom. One evening, a mysterious stranger appeared at her door, shivering and hungry. Though Celeste had little, she shared her bread and fire with the visitor.

"You have shown great kindness," the stranger said, revealing herself as the Moon Goddess. "What would you wish as your reward?"

Celeste looked at the frightened faces of her children. "I wish for light to comfort us in the darkness, so no one need fear the night."

The goddess smiled and took Celeste's most beautiful tapestry—woven with threads of silver and gold. She threw it skyward, and it shattered into a million pieces. Each fragment became a star, scattered across the heavens.

"These lights will guide travelers and comfort the afraid," declared the goddess. "And they will remind all who see them that even the smallest act of kindness can illuminate the darkness."

From that night forward, the stars have watched over humanity, born from one woman's generous heart.
